figures.caption: The characterization of the peptide LVTX-9: Table of prediction results of secondary structure of LVTX-9 (A) and diagram of the secondary structure model of LVTX-9 (B) using i-Tasser software. The red H indicates that the secondary structure is a helix. The blue S shows that the secondary structure is a strand. The black C indicates that the secondary structure is a coil. Conf. score presents the credibility of the prediction. Helical wheel structure of LVTX-9 was predicted by HeliQuest (https://heliquest.ipmc.cnrs.fr/cgi-bin/ComputParams.py, accessed on 25 July 2021) (C). Purification of LVTX-9 using RP-HPLC and the red star (*) represents the target peak (D). Identification of LVTX-9 using MALDL-TOF MS, and the molecular mass is 1851.54 (E). The cell viability of LVTX-9 on B16-F10 cells in serum-containing and non-serum-containing medium (F).
figures.label: Figure 1

figures.caption: Purification and identification of five lipopeptides using RP-HPLC and MALDL-TOF MS: The purification of (A) LVTX-9-C12, (B) LVTX-9-C14, (C) LVTX-9-C16, (D) LVTX-9-C18, and (E) LVTX-9-C20 was performed using RP-HPLC (column, Vydac, C18, 300 Å, 4.6 × 250 mm). The lipopeptides were separated at a flow rate of 1.0 mL/min under a gradient of 30–100% acetonitrile/0.1% TFA. The elution of lipopeptides was monitored at 215 nm. Identification of (F) LVTX-9-C12, (G) LVTX-9-C14, (H) LVTX-9-C16, (I) LVTX-9-C18, and (J) LVTX-9-C20 by MALDI-TOF MS, respectively. The red star (*) represents the target peak.
figures.label: Figure 2

figures.caption: Characterization of bioactivity of the lipopeptides: Cytotoxic activities of LVTX-9 and five lipopeptides in B16-F10 cells in serum-containing (A) or serum-free (B) medium as determined by CCK-8 assay (n = 3). (C) SEM images of B16-F10 cells after treatment with 50 μM of LVTX-9 or 5 μM of LVTX-9-C18. (D) LDH leakage measurement after B16-F10 cells were treated with LVTX-9 or LVTX-9-C18 at different concentrations for 24 h (n = 3). (E) Trypan blue staining images. (F) Hemolytic activity of LVTX-9 and LVTX-9-C18 against erythrocytes. Drug concentrations ranged from 1.56 to 200 µΜ. The absorbance of the supernatant was detected by microplate reader at 450 nm.
figures.label: Figure 3

figures.caption: Anti-proliferative effect of LVTX-9 and LVTX-9-C18: (A) Colony formation viability of B16-F10 cells treated with 10 μM of LVTX-9 and 1 μM of LVTX-9-C18 was evaluated by colony formation assay. (B) Quantitative results are illustrated for clonogenic assay (n = 3). Statistical analysis was performed using GraphPad software 5.0 (One-way ANOVA test). ns, non-significant, * p < 0.05.

figures.caption: Physical characteristics of LVTX-9 and LVTX-9-C18: (A) The size and zeta potential (B) of LVTX-9 and LVTX-9-C18 analyzed using DLS. figures.caption: Cytotoxicity effects of LVTX-9 and LVTX-9-C18 on B16-F10 tumor spheroids: (A) Tumor spheroid images on day 0 and day 3. (B) Volume quantitative results of tumor spheroids.
